decisions.reason: As a flagship product line very close to the firm's core practice software and supported by its own R&D and practitioner feedback, it fits the firm's strongest absorptive-capacity advantage and is likely to be further improved rather than withdrawn.

The education institute builds on the firm's training content and customer relationships, so management can absorb market feedback well, though it is somewhat less central than the core software business.

Remote screen-sharing support is closely tied to the firm's installed base and support capabilities, but because it is more of a complementary service than a distinctive core product, it has a somewhat higher withdrawal risk.

A performance analytics dashboard directly extends the firm's software, data, and workflow knowledge, making it a product the firm is well placed to refine and commercialise through learning from existing customers.
A complete practice bundle is very close to the firm's established offer and mainly repackages strong existing capabilities, so it is likely to remain on the market as a scalable sales vehicle.

A job and practice listing portal is relatively distant from the firm's core software and support knowledge base, so despite customer adjacency the firm has weaker absorptive capacity and fewer clear improvement synergies here than in its main business.
